key_insight: Biologically guided transcriptomic features outperformed unstable data-driven gene selection for predicting atezolizumab response in advanced urothelial carcinoma, especially when added beyond basic clinical data.
clinical_relevance: For immunotherapy response modeling, pathway-based transcriptomic representations may add the most value when standard biomarkers are already available, rather than relying on single-gene selection.
method: Analyzed 298 IMvigor210 patients with advanced urothelial carcinoma treated with atezolizumab.
Compared knowledge-guided tumor microenvironment gene-set features with transcriptome-wide, data-driven gene selection.
Evaluated incremental prediction gain over clinical variables, standard biomarkers, and enriched biomarker sets.
evidence_signal: Knowledge-guided features improved AUPRC by 0.058 over clinical variables alone, with smaller gains after adding standard biomarkers (+0.011) and enriched biomarkers (+0.016); external evaluation showed a similar pattern (+0.128 vs clinical alone, +0.019 vs clinical-plus-biomarker baseline).
watch_item: Data-driven gene selection was highly unstable across folds (mean Jaccard similarity 0.227), so results may be less reproducible without biologically informed feature design.
paper_title: Incremental Predictive Value and Representation of Transcriptomic Features for Immunotherapy Response in Advanced Urothelial Carcinoma
